summary.intent: Perform a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch (IPNS signature storage feature), fix all identified vulnerabilities, and merge via PR.
summary.outcome: Security review completed, 6 of 8 findings resolved (2 deferred by design), PR #448 created and pushed, though CI build failures due to ESM/CJS compatibility issues in @cipherbox/crypto required additional fix commits.

repo: @cipherbox/crypto uses tsup to dual-build ESM+CJS, but its dependencies (@libp2p/crypto, @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, ipns) are ESM-only, causing ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED when NestJS (CJS) requires the CJS build
The NestJS API is a CommonJS environment; any @cipherbox/* package it depends on must have all ESM-only transitive deps bundled into the CJS output via tsup noExternal
IPNS names are cryptographically derived from Ed25519 public keys via deriveIpnsName(); clients must verify this binding on resolve to prevent key substitution attacks from a compromised server
The web app's ipns.service.ts did not send publicKey on publish, making server-side and client-side signature verification dead code for web-published records
signatureVerified is intentionally informational — callers do not gate on it (design decision, not a bug)
The server-side pubKey validation requires @cipherbox/crypto in the API package, which was not previously a dependency

code.finding: Used spread operator Array.from(atob(...)) to convert base64 to Uint8Array — can cause call-stack overflow on large IPNS records; should use a loop-based approach instead
publicKey was not derived and sent on publish, meaning the new server-side signature storage had no public key to store for web-originated records
resolveIpnsRecord verified the Ed25519 signature but never checked that the returned pubKey actually corresponds to the requested ipnsName — allows key substitution attack by compromised server
publicKey field had @MaxLength(100) but a base64-encoded 32-byte key is 44 chars; MaxLength(70) is a tighter and correct bound
noExternal must list ALL ESM-only transitive deps (@libp2p/crypto, @libp2p/peer-id, multiformats, @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, ipns) to produce a working CJS bundle; bundleAll is the safest default

workflow: tsup noExternal is the correct fix for ESM-only deps in a dual-build package — preferable to dynamic import() workarounds which hurt readability
When adding a workspace package as a new API dependency, pnpm install must be run and the package.json updated before the API build will succeed in CI
Security review reports should be committed separately from the fixes so the report-as-written is preserved and fixes can reference it

friction: CI revealed the ESM/CJS issue only after push — not caught by local build because local Jest config likely uses ESM transform
First noExternal fix only listed 3 packages; a second CI failure revealed @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, and ipns were also ESM-only, requiring a second fix commit
The full diff was 109KB and had to be read from a persisted file path rather than inline, adding a lookup step
WebFetch of the GitHub Actions URL did not return useful log content; had to use gh CLI to get actual error messages
open_items: Finding #4 (signature verification downgrade — server can omit signature fields to bypass verification) deferred as a design decision; callers never enforce signatureVerified=true
Finding #5 (inconsistent key zeroization across crypto functions) deferred as a convention issue rather than a concrete vulnerability
The @cipherbox/crypto bundleAll approach may increase bundle size for ESM consumers — worth revisiting if tree-shaking becomes important
Server-side pubKey-to-ipnsName binding check (Medium finding #3) was added but relies on @cipherbox/crypto being available in the API at runtime — should be covered by an integration test
